title: Pitru Paksha Rules — 16 Days of Observance, Dietary Rules & What Not to Do
metaDescription: Complete guide to Pitru Paksha observance rules — dietary restrictions, forbidden activities, auspicious practices, what to do daily during the 16 days, and how to maximize ancestral merit.
author: Acharya Pandit V. K. Gayawal
keywords: what to do during Pitru Paksha
summary: Pitru Paksha is a 16-day period of ancestral reverence with specific rules for maximizing spiritual merit. This guide covers every daily observance, dietary restriction, and forbidden activity during the 16 sacred days.
content:
Pitru Paksha 2026 runs from September 7 to September 21. These 16 days have specific rules that, when followed, amplify the benefit of any ancestral ceremony performed during this period.

### Daily Morning Practice (All 16 Days)
1. Wake before sunrise
2. Take ritual bath
3. Offer water facing south (Pitru Tarpan)
4. Light a lamp (diya) for ancestors — sesame oil preferred
5. Recite Pitru Stotram or any prayer for ancestors

### Dietary Rules During Pitru Paksha

**Strictly Avoid:**
- Non-vegetarian food (meat, fish, eggs)
- Onion and garlic (rajasic foods that disturb ritual purity)
- Alcohol
- Food cooked in iron vessels (copper or clay preferred)
- Stale or reheated food
- Eating alone — always share food with others or donate first

**Recommended Foods:**
- Rice, kheer, and sattvic vegetables
- Sesame-based sweets (til ke laddoo)
- Fruits and dairy
- Food cooked with love and offered to ancestors before eating

### Activities to Avoid During Pitru Paksha
- Auspicious ceremonies (weddings, house-warming, major celebrations)
- Purchasing new major items (house, vehicle)
- Hair cutting and shaving (except on the last day)
- Nail cutting
- Starting new business ventures

### Activities Especially Meritorious During Pitru Paksha
- Feeding Brahmins and the poor
- Donating to temples
- Reading Garuda Purana in the evening
- Visiting Gaya for Pind Daan
- Offering food to crows (crows are considered vessels for ancestral souls)

faqs.question: Why are crows associated with Pitru Paksha?
faqs.answer: According to Hindu tradition, departed ancestors may visit their families in the form of crows during Pitru Paksha. Offering rice balls (kheer and rice) to crows is considered direct feeding of the ancestors. If a crow accepts the food, it is considered a positive sign that the ancestor has received the offering.
